map.Lessons 8-4, 8-5 & 8-6 — part of The Bal: Lessons 8-4, 8-5 & 8-6. Part of the arc The Balance Vault. write & graph inequalities · solution sets · 6.AT.C.9. Read it all the way. Each gate gives hints and a worked example. It does not stop you.
map.Episode 3. Same crew, same city — one fo: Episode 3. Same crew. Same city. One part of the case. Turn the page when you are set.
map.A freight lift waits at the shaft. A bra: A lift waits at the shaft. A brass plate shows the rule. The fog does not agree.
map.\"At least 12\" isn't one number. Twelve: "At least 12" is not just one number. Twelve works. Thirteen works. Fifty works. How do we write that?
map.With an inequality — a statement compari: With an inequality. It compares values. It can be true for MANY values at once.
map.Ada's manual graphs one: \"at most 20 de: Ada's book graphs one. "At most 20 degrees" is t ≤ 20. Put a FILLED circle on 20. Draw a ray to the smaller numbers. Filled means 20 counts too.
map.Symbols: > greater than · < less than ·: Signs: > greater than. < less than. ≥ at least (the number is in). ≤ at most (it is in).
map.Write the lift's rule, then pick its pic: Write the lift's rule. Then pick its picture. The fog reads signs, reader.
map.The brass plate says the lift runs with: The brass plate gives the rule. The lift runs with at least 12 crates of ballast. First, write the rule as an inequality. Let x = crates loaded. Then pick its number-line graph.
map.Conceptual: 'at least 12' means exactly: Conceptual: 'at least 12' means 12 is fine. Anything bigger is fine too. Does your sign include 12 itself?
map.Procedural: an included boundary gets a: Procedural: is the end number in? Then it gets a FILLED (closed) circle. The ray points to more values. They keep the rule true. For 'at least', that is the bigger numbers.
map.Value cards. Every card that makes the r: Value cards. A TRUE card opens a vent. Each false one… feeds the fog.
map.All the true values together form the so: All the true values make the solution set. This one is strictly less than. So the boundary is out.
map.Like loot filters. t < 4 keeps 2 and 3.5: Like loot filters. t < 4 keeps 2 and 3.5. It drops 4, because 4 < 4 is false.
map.A solution set is every value that makes: A solution set: each value that makes the statement true. An inequality can have many solutions.
map.Tap every TRUE card, reader. Miss one an: Tap each TRUE card, reader. Miss one and we keep breathing fog.
map.Vent rule: v < 9. Tap EVERY card whose v: Vent rule: v < 9. Tap EVERY card whose value makes the rule true. Those vents open. Tap a false one and the fog gets thick.
map.Conceptual: v < 9 is STRICT — a value jo: Conceptual: v < 9 is STRICT. Is a value less than 9? Only then is it in the solution set. The boundary fails its own rule: 9 < 9 is false.
map.Procedural: test the cards one at a time: Procedural: test the cards one at a time. Test decimals too. Try it with t < 4. 2 opens a vent, since 2 < 4 is true. 4.2 stays shut, since 4.2 < 4 is false.
map.The last chamber. Ada Vex's vault door —: The last room. Ada Vex's vault door. Three locks, one gauge. Fog up to the knees.
map.Balance is not stillness. It is truth, h: Balance is not standing still. It is truth, held steady. Prove three truths. Then we breathe.
map.Locks 1 and 2 are one-step equations. Lo: Locks 1 and 2 are one-step equations. Lock 3 is the gauge. The door stays open only while p ≤ 15 is true.
map.Reader — you've leveled beams and read s: Reader, you made beams level all night. You read signs too. Now call the truths!
map.Boss Gate: inverse operations on both si: Boss Gate: use inverse operations on both sides. Then test the set on the gauge. Recall what ≤ includes.
map.BOSS GATE. Three locks. The fog is liste: BOSS GATE. Three locks. The fog is listening. No stress. (Well, some.)
map.Ada's vault door. Lock 1: m − 6 = 9. Loc: Ada's vault door. Lock 1: m − 6 = 9. Lock 2: 4t = 36. Lock 3: the door stays open only while p ≤ 15 is true. Pick the set that never breaks the rule.
map.Conceptual: each lock did ONE thing to i: Conceptual: each lock did ONE thing to its variable. Undo it with the inverse, on BOTH sides. And ≤ means 'less than OR EQUAL'. So the boundary keeps the rule true.
map.Procedural: Lock 1: undo − 6 by ADDING 6: Procedural: Lock 1: undo − 6 by ADDING 6 to both sides. Lock 2: undo × 4 by DIVIDING both sides by 4. Lock 3: test EVERY number in a set on the gauge. One false number shuts the door again.
map.The fog's venting — every grate at once!: The fog goes out of each grate at once! TRUE statements, five for five!
map.And inside: Ada's eighth journal… plus t: And inside: Ada's eighth journal… and the city's books. She balanced them by hand.
map.Achievement: VAULT BREAKER. Sunrise in t: We broke the vault! The sun comes up in twenty minutes. Pancakes in thirty.
map.New distortion. The harvest dome is glow: Now a new distortion. The dome where crops grow glows wrong at night. One thing in there depends on another. To be continued…
map.The full story — The Balance Vault — is: The full story is The Balance Vault. It waits at the gate. — A.V.

map.Practice door: k − 4 = 10, then 3r = 24,: Test door: k − 4 = 10, then 3r = 24. Gauge rule: q ≤ 20.

map.x > 12 leaves 12 itself OUT — but the pl: x > 12 leaves 12 OUT. But the plate says 12 crates is enough to run.
map.x ≤ 12 points the wrong way: 'at least': x ≤ 12 points the wrong way. 'At least' lets in MORE ballast, not less.
map.x = 12 allows only exactly 12 — but 13 c: x = 12 lets in just 12. But 13 crates or 50 crates also fit 'at least 12.'
map.The symbol is right! Now pick the graph: The sign is right! Now pick the graph that shows the same thing.
map.An OPEN circle means 12 is NOT included: An OPEN circle means 12 is NOT in. But the lift runs with just 12. Look for a filled circle.
map.That ray slides toward values SMALLER th: That ray goes to values SMALLER than 12. The lift needs 12 or MORE.
map.A single point shows only x = 12. The ru: One point shows just x = 12. The rule is true for many values. Where is the ray?
map.x ≥ 12: closed circle at 12, ray to the: x ≥ 12: closed circle at 12, ray to the right. The lift hums awake. It takes the crew down.
map.Tap the cards that make v < 9 TRUE — tes: Tap the cards that make v < 9 TRUE. Test each one.
map.9 < 9 is false — the boundary stays seal: 9 < 9 is false. So the boundary stays shut. A strict < never lets its own boundary in.
map.12 < 9 is false — that card feeds the fo: 12 < 9 is false. That card feeds the fog. Just values SMALLER than 9 clear it.
map.Solution set {3, 5.5, 8.9} — three true: Solution set {3, 5.5, 8.9}. Three true statements. Three vents wide open. The room clears!
map.True values are still fogged in. EVERY c: Some true values are still in the fog. EVERY card smaller than 9 is in the solution set. Decimals too.
map.Lock 1 holds. 9 − 6 undoes the WRONG way: Lock 1 holds. 9 − 6 goes the WRONG way. m had 6 taken AWAY. So give 6 back. Add 6 to both sides.
map.Lock 1 holds. Undo − 6 with its inverse:: Lock 1 holds. Undo − 6 with its inverse: add 6 to BOTH sides.
map.Lock 2 holds. You multiplied — but 4t me: Lock 2 holds. You multiplied. But 4t means 4 × t already. Undo × 4 by dividing both sides by 4.
map.Lock 2 holds. 4t means 4 × t. Apply the: Lock 2 holds. 4t means 4 × t. Use the inverse of multiplication on both sides.
map.Two locks open! Now choose the pressure: Two locks open! Now pick the set for Lock 3.
map.Lock 3 holds. 15 ≤ 15 is true… but 16 ≤: Lock 3 holds. 15 ≤ 15 is true… but 16 ≤ 15 is FALSE. One bad number shuts the door again.
map.Lock 3 holds. 16 ≤ 15 is false and 20 ≤: Lock 3 holds. 16 ≤ 15 is false and 20 ≤ 15 is false. That set slams the door twice.
map.Lock 3 holds. 0 ≤ 15 is true, but 22 ≤ 1: Lock 3 holds. 0 ≤ 15 is true, but 22 ≤ 15 is false. EVERY number must keep the rule true.
map.ALL LOCKS OPEN. m = 15, t = 9, and {12,: ALL LOCKS OPEN. m = 15, t = 9, and {12, 15} keeps p ≤ 15 true. 15 ≤ 15 counts! The fog goes up and out. The Balance Vault gives in.
